title: 西北有高楼
titleEn: In the Northwest Stands a Tall Tower
author: 佚名（《古诗十九首》）
intro: A passer-by hears a sad song drifting down from a tower as high as the clouds. What hurts him is not the singer’s pain but that no one understands her — the poem that made 知音, “one who truly hears your music”, a lifelong Chinese ideal.
analysis: 诗人走在路上，看见西北方有一座高楼，高得和浮云一样齐，窗子雕着精美的花格，台阶有三层。楼上传来弦乐和歌声，声音非常悲伤。他猜想：能唱出这种曲子的，难道是杞梁的妻子吗？（传说杞梁战死，他的妻子痛哭十天，城墙都为她倒塌。）曲调随风飘来，弹到一半反复回旋，弹一遍就叹息好几次，激动的情绪里有说不尽的哀伤。最打动人的是“不惜歌者苦，但伤知音稀”：我不心疼唱歌的人有多苦，我难过的是能听懂她的人太少了。其实诗人自己也是一个没有知音的人，他在别人的歌声里听到了自己的孤独。最后他希望和歌者变成一对鸿鹄，一起高飞远去。“知音”的典故来自伯牙和钟子期，这首诗让“知音难得”成了中国人反复吟咏的主题。
analysisEn: Walking along, the poet sees a tower in the northwest, so tall it seems level with the drifting clouds, with finely carved lattice windows and three flights of steps. From high up comes the sound of strings and a voice singing — terribly sad. Who could make such music, he wonders — someone like the wife of Qi Liang? (Legend says that when Qi Liang died in battle, his wife wept for ten days until a city wall collapsed.) The clear notes float down on the wind; halfway through, the melody circles back again and again; after each phrase the singer sighs, and beneath the strong feeling there is grief that will not end. Then the key couplet: “I don’t grieve for the singer’s suffering; I grieve that so few truly understand her.” The poet, we realise, is lonely in just the same way: in a stranger’s song he hears his own isolation. He ends with a wish that the two of them could become a pair of great swans and fly away together. The idea of the 知音, the friend who truly “knows your music”, goes back to the legend of Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi; this poem made “how rare a true listener is” a theme Chinese poets returned to again and again.
background: The Nineteen Old Poems (古诗十九首) are anonymous five-character poems from the late Eastern Han (2nd century AD), collected in the Wen Xuan anthology. Many are thought to be by educated men frustrated in their careers, far from home; one early anthology, the Yutai Xinyong, credits this poem to Mei Cheng, but most scholars treat it as anonymous.
pronunciation: 阿阁 ē gé（不读 ā）；三重 chóng；谁能为此曲 wéi；无乃 wú nǎi；杞梁 qǐ liáng；中曲 zhōng qǔ；一弹 tán；不惜 xī；鸿鹄 hóng hú（鹄不读 gào、hào）；愿为 wéi。机器朗读的“阿”“重”已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字。
version: 采用《文选》所收《古诗十九首》第五首的通行文本，全诗十六句。末句《文选》作“双鸣鹤”，《玉台新咏》作“双鸿鹄”，今通行本多用“鸿鹄”；“窗”“弦”古本或作“牕”“絃”。

lines.zh: 西北有高楼，上与浮云齐。
lines.rhythm: 西北/有高楼，上与/浮云齐
lines.py: xī běi yǒu gāo lóu, shàng yǔ fú yún qí
lines.lit: In the northwest there is a tall tower; its top is level with the floating clouds.
lines.en: Far to the northwest a tower rises, tall enough to touch the drifting clouds.

lines.zh: 交疏结绮窗，阿阁三重阶。
lines.rhythm: 交疏/结绮窗，阿阁/三重阶
lines.py: jiāo shū jié qǐ chuāng, ē gé sān chóng jiē
lines.lit: Criss-cross lattices on patterned windows; a four-eaved hall above triple steps.
lines.en: Its windows are carved in delicate lattice; its hall sits high above three flights of steps.
lines.tts: 交疏结绮窗，婀阁三崇阶。

lines.zh: 上有弦歌声，音响一何悲！
lines.rhythm: 上有/弦歌声，音响/一何悲
lines.py: shàng yǒu xián gē shēng, yīn xiǎng yī hé bēi
lines.lit: From above comes the sound of strings and singing; how sad the sound is!
lines.en: From up there comes a song with strings — and oh, how sad it sounds.

lines.zh: 谁能为此曲？无乃杞梁妻。
lines.rhythm: 谁能/为此曲，无乃/杞梁妻
lines.py: shuí néng wéi cǐ qǔ, wú nǎi qǐ liáng qī
lines.lit: Who could make this tune? Could it be the wife of Qi Liang?
lines.en: Who could make music like this? Someone, perhaps, like Qi Liang’s grieving widow.

lines.zh: 清商随风发，中曲正徘徊。
lines.rhythm: 清商/随风发，中曲/正徘徊
lines.py: qīng shāng suí fēng fā, zhōng qǔ zhèng pái huái
lines.lit: The clear shang notes rise on the wind; in the middle of the tune, it lingers back and forth.
lines.en: The clear, cold notes drift out on the wind; halfway through, the melody wavers and circles.

lines.zh: 一弹再三叹，慷慨有余哀。
lines.rhythm: 一弹/再三叹，慷慨/有余哀
lines.py: yī tán zài sān tàn, kāng kǎi yǒu yú āi
lines.lit: One strum, then sighs again and again; deeply stirred, with grief left over.
lines.en: Every phrase she plays is followed by sighs; her feeling runs high, and sorrow lingers after.

lines.zh: 不惜歌者苦，但伤知音稀。
lines.rhythm: 不惜/歌者苦，但伤/知音稀
lines.py: bù xī gē zhě kǔ, dàn shāng zhī yīn xī
lines.lit: I do not pity the singer’s pain; I only grieve that those who understand the music are few.
lines.en: It isn’t her pain that hurts me most — it’s that so few can truly hear her.

lines.zh: 愿为双鸿鹄，奋翅起高飞。
lines.rhythm: 愿为/双鸿鹄，奋翅/起高飞
lines.py: yuàn wéi shuāng hóng hú, fèn chì qǐ gāo fēi
lines.lit: I wish we were a pair of great swans, beating our wings and rising high.
lines.en: If only we were two wild swans, beating our wings and rising together into the sky.

words.note: 现代汉语仍用，也比喻不重要的东西，如“过眼浮云”。
绮：有花纹的丝织品，这里形容窗格精美。

words.en: a hall with eaves on all four sides

words.note: 重：层，现代汉语“重重叠叠”。
古汉语推测语气，相当于“莫非”“恐怕是”。

words.en: the wife of Qi Liang, who wept down a city wall
words.note: 后来演变成“孟姜女哭长城”的故事。
古代乐调名，声音清越悲凉。

words.en: to linger, go back and forth
words.note: 现代汉语仍用，多指人来回走。
古义指情绪激昂；今天多指大方，如“慷慨解囊”。

words.en: to pity; to feel sorry about
one who truly understands (you / your music)
words.note: 来自伯牙、钟子期的故事；今天仍常说“知音难觅”。
今天“鸿鹄之志”比喻远大的志向。

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: 高耸入云的楼，可望而不可即，就像那位难以接近、无人理解的歌者。
imagery.en: A tower reaching the clouds — visible but out of reach, like the singer no one can come close to or understand.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: “上与浮云齐”，写楼之高，也带出远离人间的孤独感。
imagery.en: Level with the clouds: the tower’s height also suggests loneliness, far above the ordinary world.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 化作一对鸿鹄高飞，是知音相伴、摆脱孤独的理想。
imagery.en: Becoming a pair of high-flying swans is his dream of escaping loneliness with someone who understands.
